title: Ephemeral KV Cache Data Retention Clause - Draft
body:
Purpose:
This draft provides supplier-side contractual language and operational guidance addressing retention, access, and deletion of ephemeral key-value (KV) cache data generated during managed inference. The goal is to ensure minimal residual data risk for customer queries while preserving necessary caching behavior for latency/cost optimization.

Context / why this matters:
- Modern LLM serving uses KV caches (attention/key-value caches, prefix caches, session slices) to accelerate generation.
- KV caches can transiently contain fragments of customer input, prompts, or derived representations that may include PII or confidential content.
- Unlike long-term logs, KV caches are typically ephemeral but may persist across process restarts, snapshots, or crash-induced core dumps. Contractual clarity is required so customers can rely on technical controls and have audit evidence.

Definitions (for insertion into DPA or Master Services Agreement):
- "Ephemeral KV Cache": in-memory or local on-disk artifacts maintained by Supplier's inference runtime that store model-key/value pairs, intermediate activations, or retained prompt prefixes used to accelerate token generation, with expected short lifetimes measured in seconds to hours.
- "Customer Sensitive Content": any Customer Data as defined in the DPA that includes PII, PHI, or Proprietary Information.
- "Volatile Storage": memory-resident storage that is not intended to be persisted beyond the life of the process or session.

Sample Contract Clause (Tiered, pick one for negotiation):
1) Minimal / Default (for self-serve/hosted customers):
"Supplier shall ensure that Ephemeral KV Cache contents are retained only for the duration necessary to complete the associated inference session and, absent legal hold, are automatically purged within one hour of session termination. Supplier shall not persist Ephemeral KV Cache to durable external logs or backups except where strictly necessary for debugging; any such persistence must be encrypted and retained no longer than 30 days and Customer shall be notified and given the option to request deletion. Supplier will implement reasonable technical controls to avoid KV cache contents being captured in persistent crash dumps; where crash-dump persistence occurs Supplier will delete such artifacts within 72 hours of discovery unless retention is required by law."

2) Enterprise / Private Deployment (stronger guarantees):
"Supplier shall operate Ephemeral KV Cache in volatile memory only and shall not write KV cache artifacts to disk, snapshot storage, or external object stores. If Supplier's runtime requires momentary disk-assisted spill for memory pressure, Supplier will use ephemeral containers with encrypted tmpfs and ensure files are zeroed and unlinked immediately upon session end. Supplier will provide Customer with configuration options to set maximum KV Cache TTL (including immediate purge on session end) and an API endpoint to request immediate invalidation of KV cache shards associated with a Customer's tenancy. Proof of deletion shall be provided on request in the form of a tamper-evident log entry and runtime trace showing cache invalidation operations."

3) High Assurance (regulated workloads):
"Supplier shall offer a deployment mode (e.g., Private or Dedicated) where KV caching is disabled by default or run with deterministic, auditable in-memory-only caches. In this mode Supplier will: (a) never leak KV cache to any diagnostic or monitoring pipeline; (b) provide Customer with cryptographic attestation (HSM-backed) that caches were zeroed after session termination; and (c) retain no recovery snapshots that include KV cache. Supplier will also agree to periodic third-party audits of cache handling controls."

Operational Obligations (to include in Schedule/Appendix):
- Default TTL: supplier to state default ephemeral retention (recommended: 15 minutes) and maximum allowed (negotiable).
- Purge semantics: describe immediate in-process zeroing vs. asynchronous garbage collection; provide guarantee window for full deletion.
- Crash-dump controls: list steps to avoid or scrub caches in any post-mortem artifacts and timeline for remediation.
- Encryption/Access controls: caches in memory are protected by process privileges; any on-disk spill must be encrypted with customer-scoped keys or supplier-managed keys with documented rotation.
- Evidence & logging: supplier to maintain an audit trail for cache invalidation requests and automated purges (logs must not contain cache contents). Logs retained per normal operational logging retention schedule.

Data Minimization & Anonymization Recommendations (negotiable technical requirements):
- Token filtering: supplier should strip or hash known identifiers before storing into cache when possible (configurable).
- Prefix scrubbing: for prompt caching, store fingerprinted prefixes rather than raw text unless customer opts-in.
- Opt-out toggle: customer can request disables for caching per-tenant or per-route.

Breach & Incident Language (insert into incident response exhibit):
"If Supplier discovers unauthorized access to Ephemeral KV Cache that may have exposed Customer Sensitive Content, Supplier shall: (i) notify Customer within 48 hours; (ii) purge impacted cache shards and any persisted crash artifacts immediately; (iii) provide findings, scope, and mitigation steps; and (iv) preserve forensic evidence for 30 days or as otherwise agreed subject to legal constraints. Supplier's notification obligations do not limit Customer's rights under the DPA or applicable law."

Proofs & Auditability (practical items to include):
- Runtime trace samples showing cache allocation/invalidation timestamps (redacted, never containing raw cache content).
- CI test vectors demonstrating that cache purge endpoints result in measurable memory-free events.
- Configuration exports showing TTLs, per-tenant toggles, and spill-to-disk disabled state.
- For private deployments: host-level scripts/commands used to flush caches and hashes of zeroed pages.

Negotiation Checklist (for legal + security):
- Decide default TTL and maximum retention ceiling.
- Determine whether spills to disk are allowed; if yes, encryption key ownership and retention.
- Add customer control (API toggle) for per-tenant cache disablement.
- Agree SLAs for purge operations (e.g., immediate purge < 5s, full deletion within X hours).
- Evidence format for deletion proofs.

Implementation Notes for Engineering (draft ops guidance to attach to clause):
- Use tmpfs for any required spill, mount with nodev,nosuid,noexec and encrypt at filesystem layer when required.
- Harden process to reduce core dump generation; set ulimit -c 0 where feasible or configure core_pattern to a secure sink.
- Integrate cache purge API into customer control plane and require RBAC logs for requests.
- Add periodic memory-scan tests to CI that assert no stale caches remain after session termination.

Open Questions / Risks (working items):
- How to provide cryptographic attestation for in-memory zeroing without exposing raw material? (possible approaches: attest sequence of zeroing operations captured by TPM/HSM with sequence hash).
- Performance trade-offs for disabling caching vs latency/cost — need benchmark matrix for typical session lengths.
- Crash-dump handling is implementation-specific across distros and orchestrators; map exact remediation steps for each supported runtime.

Recommended next steps:
- Legal to include the "Minimal / Default" clause in the standard DPA with an appendix option for Enterprise/High-Assurance alternatives.
- Security & Eng to prepare a short runbook that maps the contractual language to concrete runtime knobs and audit artifacts (owner: Marco Nguyen).
- Product to add cache control toggles in the tenant settings UI and expose a purge API (owner: Priya Shah).
- Create a short customer-facing FAQ describing what "Ephemeral KV Cache" means and available options.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working draft intended for negotiation with security-conscious customers. Language is purposefully prescriptive in the Enterprise variants to accelerate enterprise procurement; technical artifacts referenced (attestations, runtime traces) should be validated by SRE/infra before finalizing.
